title: dnaa-3 DnaA-box occupancy by region — reproduced on the dnaa-4 reference config (linear s=0.6 + F-05)
caption: Five-timepoint chromosome-map snapshots across the succinate cell cycle, rendered from the dnaa-4 autoregulation REFERENCE run (dnaa4_s06_F05_seed1_12gen) — i.e. the SAME configuration and parameters as dnaa-4 (linear autoregulation s=0.6 + F-05, V=1.5e-3, k_h=0.025/min, K_d 3/100 nM), per Rashmi 2026-06-16. oriC carries 11 boxes (3 high-affinity + 8 low-affinity) at cell birth (one chromosome) and DOUBLES to 22 at replication (two oriC) — the snapshot labels read 2/11 -> 6/11 -> 11/22 -> 7/22 -> 6/22, correcting the prior chart that wrongly showed 22 at t=0. Filled = DnaA-bound, open ring = free; red square = ter. Bottom panel: in-sim free DnaA-ATP (nM, black) vs the 100 nM oriC-low K_d (red dashed), with oriC-LOW (green) and oriC-HIGH (purple dashed) occupancy tracked SEPARATELY on the right axis (Rashmi's request).
interpretation: On the dnaa-4 reference config the box binding reproduces correctly: the oriC site count is right (11 at birth -> 22 at replication), and the low-affinity over-binding is resolved — oriC-low occupancy fills gradually early in the cycle (to ~0.38) then de-occupies to ~0.06 as free DnaA-ATP falls well below the 100 nM K_d (~5-50 nM), while the high-affinity pool stays near-saturated (~0.7-1.0). Tracking low-affinity separately (Rashmi 2026-06-16) makes the gradual fill-then-empty dynamic explicit rather than lumping it with the always-full high-affinity sites.
